study type: secondary analysis of a cross-sectional survey
cohort: The study included 167,380 mother-child pairs from India, where children were under five years of age and paired at the household level.
finding: The prevalence of double burden of malnutrition (DBM) was 7.7% and triple burden of malnutrition (TBM) was 5.1% among mother-child dyads in India, with various sociodemographic and child-related factors, including birth weight, associated with both.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was identified as a factor associated with both double and triple burden of malnutrition.
